newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil flat to weaker in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil flat to weaker in thin volume.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures were flat to weaker in early trading, while refined products traded mixed to weaker, as the market quietly drifted into the weekend, brokers said.
At 1100 EDT, July crude was off 5 cents at $20.92 a barrel, tracking a tight range between $21.05 and $20.86.
July unleaded gasoline was down 0.40 cent at 62.85 cents a gallon. July heating oil was unchanged at 56.02 cents.
Floor brokers saw little direction in Friday's trading, with most expecting an aimless day of consolidation after Thursday's technically led rally.
July crude gained 18 cents a barrel Thursday after rising as much as 47 cents as speculative jumped in the market when favorable technical indicators were seen, traders said.
"With it being Friday, the market seems to be stalled," one trader said.
Spot-contract expirations in unleaded and heating should keep products futures on the defensive as spread trading and liquiudation in the June contracts distort the board for a day.
In their last trading session, June unleaded gas was 0.75 cent lower and almost motionless while June heating oil was 0.30 cent firmer.
